newsitem.title: UK: William Baird to restructure, take charge.
newsitem.headline: William Baird to restructure, take charge.

text.p: William Baird Plc said on Thursday it planned to divest its contract clothing businesses that supply retailers other than Marks and Spencer Plc and also take a charge for the restructuring.
The clothing company said it would make a provision of between 23.6 million stg and 28.6 million in the current year to cover stock and asset writedowns.
As part of the provision, about 5.0 million stg was earmarked for site consolidation, cost reductions and moves into offshore clothing manufacturing.
William Baird said in a statement that it estimated the cash cost of the restructuring programme at some 3.6 million stg, with payback expected within two years.
The company also said it would make a provision of 5.5 million stg mainly for the accelerated disposal of excess stocks to reduce working capital.
William Baird said the divestment of its non-core businesses may result in a loss on disposal of 10 to 15 million stg.
In addition, 3.1 million stg of goodwill, previously written off to reserves, was expected to be charged back through the company's profit and loss account.
The firm said it would focus on its own clothing brands and designing and making contract clothing for Marks and Spencer.
William Baird also said it expected to flatten its management structure, with all of its major businesses reporting directly to recently-appointed chief executive David Suddens.

"Following the reorganisation, William Baird will be in better shape to grow with Marks and Spencer and also in those clothing markets in the UK and overseas which offer greater growth potential," the company said.
